method.title: How these figures are measured
method.successRate: Backup success rate: succeeded runs divided by succeeded and failed runs that finished in the period. Cancelled runs were stopped on purpose and are not counted.
method.volume: Protected data is the newest backup of every protected object. Stored bytes are the encrypted, deduplicated pack files; packs removed by garbage collection no longer appear in earlier intervals.
method.dedup: Deduplication ratio: all retained backups added up, divided by the bytes stored.
method.readiness: Proven restorable: objects whose newest backup was rated “Ready” or “Attention” by a restore check of that very backup. A backup taken after the last check stays unproven until it is checked itself; objects never checked or never backed up are not proven, and damage the storage check finds after a check counts as not restorable.
method.status: Excluded objects are not protected and objects removed from their source count while they still have a backup. Only an object's current status is stored, so an object excluded today is left out of earlier intervals too.
method.throttling: Throttling waits are what Microsoft Graph imposed on finished runs; {appName} waits as long as Microsoft asks instead of retrying sooner.

backup.failed: A backup run of a mailbox, OneDrive, IMAP account, server or client did not finish.
backup.overdue: A mailbox, OneDrive, IMAP account, machine or guest (VM or container) had no successful backup for longer than its backup jobs plan (twice the longest gap of the schedules, two days without one), or for longer than the rule's own deadline. Once per object, until a backup succeeds again.
backup.succeeded: A backup run of a mailbox, OneDrive, IMAP account or file share finished. Every run, so best for a channel that wants to see each one.
backup.suspicious: What a backup of a machine, file share, Proxmox VE guest, mailbox or OneDrive saw looks like ransomware at work: far more changes than usual, mass deletions or renamed extensions, known ransomware names or files that look encrypted. Once per object until a restore point without findings follows or the finding is marked as a false alarm. Retention of the object pauses until an administrator resolves the finding.
backup.suspicious_hold: Retention of a machine, file share, Proxmox VE guest, mailbox or OneDrive has been paused for a while (14 days by default) because of a suspicious restore point nobody resolved. No restore point of it is deleted, so its storage keeps growing. Repeated at the same interval until an administrator marks the finding as a false alarm or releases the hold.

restore.failed: A restore or a download, of a server or client too, could not be finished.
restore.completed: A restore or download is ready.

archive.failed: An archive sync run did not finish.

directory.failed: Reading users and mailboxes from Microsoft 365 failed.

verify.red: A restore would not be complete: the newest backup of a mailbox, OneDrive, IMAP account, server or client failed its restore check.
verify.recovered: A mailbox, OneDrive, IMAP account, server or client that was red or yellow is green again.
verify.completed: A restore check finished, whatever its rating. Every check, so best for a channel that wants to see each one.

boot_test.failed: A Proxmox VE restore point did not boot: restoring it to a temporary guest, starting it or its boot failed.
boot_test.unproven: A VM restored from a Proxmox VE restore point started and kept running, but its QEMU Guest Agent never answered, so nothing proves the system inside works.

scrub.corrupt: The storage check found damaged or missing pack files.
scrub.repaired: Damaged pack files were restored from an intact copy.

endpoint.stale: A server has not reported for more than two hours, or a client has had no good backup for several days.
endpoint.suspicious_snapshot: A snapshot appeared that no backup run reported, or one dated in the future. Retention keeps it; the machine may be compromised.
endpoint.storage_quota: The backup data of a machine, or all of a tenant's together, reached 90 percent of the storage budget, or backups were refused because it is used up.
endpoint.repository_locked: Retention and checks kept finding a machine's backup data locked for more than twelve hours.

file_share.storage_quota: The backup data of a file share, or all of a tenant's shares together, reached 80 percent of the storage budget, or new backups are refused because it is used up.
file_share.repository_locked: Retention and checks kept finding a file share's backup data locked for more than twelve hours.

update.available: A newer version of the software is available. Raised once per version for the whole installation, so only provider administrators can choose it.

installation.disk_low: The disk under the database or under the local default repository has less than a tenth of its size free (and less than 5 GiB). Raised once until the disk recovers, for the whole installation, so only provider administrators can choose it.
installation.app_secret_expiring: Warns before the client secret or certificate of the central Microsoft 365 app registration expires: 30 days before, again 7 days before, and once it has expired. Only when its expiry is known. Raised for the whole installation, so only provider administrators can choose it.

source.app_secret_expiring: Warns before the client secret or certificate of a Microsoft 365 source's own app expires: 30 days before, again 7 days before, and once it has expired. Only for sources whose expiry is known (the date noted for the secret, or the certificate's own end). Once it has expired, backups of the source fail until a new secret or certificate is entered.

object.inactive: Once per object when {appName} stops backing it up because the source no longer has it, the account is disabled or unlicensed, or Microsoft locked the OneDrive or site. Also once per IMAP account when its login has been refused for several days and an answer is needed whether the account was shut down. Not a failure: confirm or answer under Protection.
object.inactive_many: One warning instead of many notices when more than 10 objects, or more than 20% of a tenant's protected objects, stop being backed up within a day, for example because licences were removed or the sync scope is wrong. The same for IMAP accounts whose login questions are raised at once, for example after the source's password changed.
